children: , the global drug and biotechnology company, secured exclusive worldwide rights to products from its expanded Gate Bioscience partnership, while shares traded around $1,161.50, up approximately 1.6%, as of 11:43 a.m. ET Tuesday. The prize is access to potential medicines aimed at proteins that have proved tough to tackle. But this is a discovery deal. Revenue is still a long way off.

The expansion adds one target and leaves room for a second. According to Gate's announcement, potential payments could exceed $870 million if milestones are achieved; the upfront payment was not disclosed. Gate handles discovery. Lilly takes responsibility for later preclinical development, human trials, manufacturing and commercialization. The small molecules are designed to stop selected disease-causing proteins from progressing through a cellular secretion channel, triggering their degradation.

The valuation graphic puts shares 25.91% below the roughly $1,570 GF Value estimate, suggesting a valuation cushion rather than guaranteed upside. The partnership offers another route to expand Lilly's pipeline, but the headline deal value is no measure of likely returns. Milestone payments tie much of the potential cost to progress, while research funding and an upfront payment still require capital today. Investors need successful drug candidates and convincing clinical results before this early science becomes a meaningful earnings story.

title: Lilly Stock Rises as $870 Million Gate Deal Adds One Target
